stories.title: Nikkei discloses third data breach in a month, 1.8M records exposed
stories.summary: Nikkei Inc. disclosed a new data breach, the third in about a month, that exposed 1.83 million personal information records.
stories.explanation: Nikkei Inc. suffered three separate data breaches within one month, exposing 1.83 million records of personal information. This matters because repeated breaches in a short timeframe suggest the company's security controls aren't working effectively and attackers may still have access. Defenders respond by conducting a full security investigation to find and close how attackers got in, notifying affected people, and rebuilding defenses to prevent future incidents.

stories.title: 970,000 Medi-Cal Members Affected by Paradigm Healthcare Data Breach
stories.summary: Paradigm Healthcare Services detected an intrusion in October 2025, but it took nearly a year to start notifying affected individuals.
stories.explanation: Paradigm Healthcare Services discovered a data breach in October 2025 but waited nearly a year before notifying the 970,000 affected Medi-Cal members—a health insurance program in California. Delayed notifications prevent people from protecting themselves against identity theft or fraud. Defenders and regulators typically require breach notifications within 30–60 days, and delays like this trigger investigations and potential fines for violating privacy laws.

stories.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
stories.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.
stories.explanation: U.S. federal investigators found that people working at ransomware negotiation firms (companies hired to communicate with attackers) had unusually close ties to the ShinyHunters hacking group, which stole sensitive data from the FBI. This matters because it suggests possible corruption—negotiators may be tipping off attackers or helping them profit. Defenders respond by scrutinizing third-party vendors, checking for conflicts of interest, and improving controls over who handles sensitive communications.

stories.title: OpenCode hack exposes API keys amid AI distillation attacks
stories.summary: The open-source AI coding project OpenCode has notified a small number of users that API keys they used with external providers were exposed in a security breach.
stories.explanation: The OpenCode open-source project suffered a breach that exposed API keys—secret credentials used to access external services like cloud providers or third-party APIs. Exposed API keys let attackers impersonate the legitimate service and steal data or cause damage without authorization. Defenders rotate (replace) the keys immediately, review logs for misuse, and implement monitoring to catch unauthorized access attempts.

stories.title: GhostAction Attackers Plant Credential Stealer Disguised as Font in 94 GitHub Repositories
stories.summary: The threat actor behind the GhostAction supply chain attack has expanded beyond injecting malicious GitHub Actions workflows into compromised projects to phish open-source developers and deliver a stealer malware disguised within a fake font file. The latest evolution, detailed by OpenSourceMalware, signals that the attackers are actively refining their modus operandi in response to steps
stories.explanation: Attackers behind GhostAction compromised 94 GitHub repositories (code storage sites) by planting malware hidden inside a fake font file to trick developers into downloading it and stealing their login credentials. This matters because developers often have access to sensitive code and systems, so stealing their credentials gives attackers a foothold in major organizations. Defenders warn developers to verify downloads, scan files before use, and limit what permissions each person needs.

stories.title: Drupal Warns of Fast Exploitation Risk for Critical Core RCE Flaw
stories.summary: Critical flaws impact the Entity List and Field UI modules, and exploit paths exist with contributed modules.
stories.explanation: Drupal, a widely-used website platform, warned users about critical vulnerabilities (serious flaws) in its Entity List and Field UI modules that allow remote code execution (RCE—running attacker commands on the server) and can be exploited quickly. This matters because attackers can take control of websites using Drupal without needing valid login credentials. Defenders immediately apply security patches (updates), scan for signs of exploitation, and temporarily disable vulnerable modules if updates aren't available.

stories.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: 98 Zero-Days, Rogue AI Agents, $100M Crypto Theft, 700 Supermarkets Hit and More
stories.summary: The worst problems don't always come with a warning. Sometimes they arrive through a service everyone trusts, a device someone bought, or a system nobody thought to check. By the time something looks wrong, the damage may already be done. This week had plenty of that. Trusted connections became a problem. Hardware wasn't as safe as it looked. Old bugs found new victims, and some systems were
stories.explanation: This recap summarizes a particularly bad week in cybersecurity with 98 zero-day vulnerabilities (flaws unknown to vendors), rogue AI agents, a $100 million cryptocurrency theft, and attacks on 700 supermarkets—all with minimal warning. This matters because not every threat arrives as a dramatic headline; some arrive through trusted services or devices that people didn't suspect were compromised. Defenders focus on continuous monitoring and assuming any system could be attacked, rather than waiting for obvious warning signs.

stories.title: Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses npm Packages to Spread Malware and Hijack AI Agent Traffic
stories.summary: A fake Web3 accelerator has been observed pushing information stealers and backdoors to Windows and macOS systems using malicious npm packages under the pretext of offering free artificial intelligence (AI) credits for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini, coding tools, and security audits. "The tools delivered information-stealing malware and backdoors for macOS and Windows machines," Elastic
stories.explanation: Attackers created a fake Web3 accelerator (a fake startup funding program) and distributed malware through npm packages (free code libraries) claiming to offer free AI credits for tools like Claude and Google Gemini. This matters because developers trust npm packages and use them routinely, making it an effective distribution channel to compromise developer machines and steal credentials or install backdoors (hidden entrances for attackers). Defenders implement package verification processes, scan dependencies for malware, and limit what packages can access.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: ISC BIND is DNS software (the system that translates domain names to IP addresses) and CVE-2015-5477 is a flaw that causes data processing errors, making DNS unreliable or crashable. This matters because DNS is fundamental to internet operations; breaking it disrupts services broadly. Defenders apply vendor patches, use redundant DNS servers, and monitor for abnormal query patterns.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: ProFTPD is file transfer software and CVE-2015-3306 is a flaw where the access control system fails to properly restrict who can do what. This matters because unrestricted file access lets attackers read, modify, or delete sensitive files. Defenders update software, implement role-based permissions, and audit file access logs.

cves.name: Apache Struts Command Injection Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: Apache Struts is a web application framework and CVE-2016-3081 is a command injection flaw—a vulnerability where untrusted user input is executed as system commands. This matters because attackers can run arbitrary code on the server, leading to full system compromise. Defenders patch immediately, validate all user input, and use security filters to block malicious commands.

cves.name: Ivanti Connect Secure Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: Ivanti Connect Secure is remote access software and CVE-2026-104935 allows attackers to bypass authentication (login checks) by spoofing—faking their identity without knowing the real password. This matters because it lets unauthorized users gain access to the network and internal systems. Defenders implement additional verification layers, monitor for unusual login patterns, and restrict network access to trusted sources.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: ONLYOFFICE Docs Server is a document editing platform and CVE-2021-3199 is a path traversal flaw—a vulnerability where attackers access files outside the intended directory by using special path tricks (like '../../../'). This matters because attackers can read sensitive files like configuration files or credentials. Defenders update the software, restrict file system permissions, and implement input validation to block malicious paths.
